died of grief and illness in office

units.zh: 林培厚，字敏齋，浙江瑞安人。
units.en: Lin Peihou, whose style was Minzhai, came from Rui'an in Zhejiang.
units.literal: Lin Peihou, style Minzhai, was a native of Rui'an in Zhejiang.

units.zh: 嘉慶十三年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。
units.en: He earned his jinshi degree in the thirteenth year of the Jiaqing reign, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

units.zh: 出為四川重慶知府。
units.en: He was then posted as prefect of Chongqing in Sichuan.
units.literal: He went out to serve as prefect of Chongqing in Sichuan.

units.zh: 啯匪帶刀異常制，禁鍛者毋制賣，有犯則坐。
units.en: Because bandits went about armed in defiance of the usual rules, he forbade smiths to forge and sell blades without restriction, and punished anyone who violated the ban.
units.literal: Bandits carrying knives beyond the usual regulations were targeted; smiths were forbidden to forge and sell blades without restriction, and violators were prosecuted.

units.zh: 沿江渡船為盜資，籍而稽其出入，刻姓名船側，盜為衰息。
units.en: River ferries had been a resource for bandits, so he registered them, inspected their traffic, and had names carved on each hull; piracy then subsided.
units.literal: Ferry boats along the river supplied bandits; he registered them and checked their comings and goings, carved names on the sides of boats, and banditry declined.

units.zh: 民習天主教，搜其書，批抉繆妄，聞者多悔悟。
units.en: The populace had taken up Catholicism; he seized their books, refuted their errors point by point, and many listeners came to their senses.
units.literal: The people were accustomed to Catholicism; he searched out their books, exposed errors and absurdities, and many who heard him repented.

units.zh: 署川東道，所屬雷波廳民、夷忿爭，或覬覦邀功，請發兵，培厚不應，立縛治其魁，餘悉貸遣。
units.en: While serving as acting intendant of eastern Sichuan, he faced a bitter feud between Han settlers and Yi people in Leibo; some officials, eager for glory, urged him to send troops. He refused, swiftly seized and punished the ringleaders, and released the rest with clemency.
units.literal: While acting as intendant of eastern Sichuan, in his subordinate Leibo subprefecture Han and Yi people quarreled in anger; some coveted merit and asked for troops. Peihou would not agree, immediately bound and punished the ringleaders, and pardoned and released the rest.

units.zh: 總督蔣攸銛器之，稱為蜀中良吏之最。
units.en: Governor-General Jiang Youxian held him in high regard and pronounced him the finest administrator in Sichuan.
units.literal: Governor-General Jiang Youxian valued him and called him the finest good official in Shu.

units.zh: 母憂歸，服闋，授直隸天津府。
units.en: After returning home to mourn his mother and completing the mourning period, he was appointed prefect of Tianjin in Zhili.
units.literal: He returned home on his mother's death; when mourning ended he was appointed to Tianjin prefecture in Zhili.

units.zh: 畿輔大水，天津地窪下，災尤劇，培厚遍行屬縣，賑活饑民七萬有奇。
units.en: When catastrophic floods struck the capital region, Tianjin—lying low—suffered worst of all. Peihou toured every county under his jurisdiction and kept more than seventy thousand starving people alive through relief work.
units.literal: The capital region suffered great floods; Tianjin's land was low and the disaster especially severe. Peihou traveled through all subordinate counties and relieved more than seventy thousand starving people.

units.zh: 奉天、台灣商米先後抵海口，議以官錢收買，委曲劑量，商民交利，而官不費。
units.en: Commercial grain shipments from Fengtian and Taiwan reached the port in succession; he proposed buying them with public funds, carefully calibrating quantities so merchants and commoners alike benefited while the treasury spent nothing extra.
units.literal: Merchant grain from Fengtian and Taiwan successively reached the port; it was proposed to buy with official funds, carefully measured and adjusted, so merchants and people both profited while the government spent nothing.

units.zh: 時蔣攸銛移督直隸，詔舉賢吏，遂薦之，不旬日，擢大順廣道。
units.en: Jiang Youxian had by then been transferred to govern Zhili; when the throne called for nominations of capable officials, he recommended Peihou, who within ten days was promoted intendant of the Da-Shun-Guang circuit.
units.literal: At that time Jiang Youxian was transferred to govern Zhili; an edict called for recommending worthy officials, and he recommended Peihou; within ten days Peihou was promoted to Da-Shun-Guang circuit intendant.

units.zh: 畿南澇後，大興水利。
units.en: After the floods in southern Zhili, he launched a major program of hydraulic works.
units.literal: After flooding in southern Zhili, waterworks were greatly promoted.

units.zh: 培厚先在天津治淀河，至大名治新衛河、洺河，浚築悉中程度。
units.en: Peihou had first regulated the Dian River at Tianjin; at Daming he took charge of the new Wei and Ming rivers, and in every case his dredging and construction met the required standard.
units.literal: Peihou had first at Tianjin managed the Dian River; at Daming he managed the new Wei River and the Ming River; dredging and construction all hit the proper standard.

units.zh: 培厚數以時事利病、屬吏賢否語攸銛，為布政使屠之申所忌。
units.en: Peihou frequently reported to Jiang Youxian on the strengths and weaknesses of current policies and on the merit of subordinate officials, which earned him the enmity of Provincial Treasurer Tu Zhishen.
units.literal: Peihou often told Youxian about the advantages and harms of current affairs and whether subordinate officials were worthy; he was resented by provincial treasurer Tu Zhishen.

units.zh: 及攸銛入相，那彥成代之，坐河北旱荒施賑不如法，解培厚任，宣宗夙知其能，改授湖北糧儲道。
units.en: After Jiang Youxian joined the Grand Council, Na Yancheng succeeded him as governor-general; Peihou was dismissed on the pretext that his drought relief in Hebei had not followed proper procedure, but the Xuanzong Emperor, who had long valued his talent, reassigned him as grain intendant of Hubei.
units.literal: When Youxian entered the Grand Council, Na Yancheng replaced him; Peihou was removed from office on the charge that relief during Hebei's drought and famine had not followed regulations, but the Xuanzong Emperor had long known his ability and reassigned him grain intendant of Hubei.

units.zh: 時河患淺涸，漕舟數阻。
units.en: The river had grown shallow and dry, and grain transports were repeatedly stalled.
units.literal: At the time the river suffered shallowing and drying, and grain transport boats were repeatedly blocked.

units.zh: 攸銛以大學士出督兩江，期八省漕以首夏畢渡河，乘清水盛漲，浮渡遄利。
units.en: Jiang Youxian went out as Grand Secretary to supervise the Two Jiangs, aiming to move the grain fleets of eight provinces across the river by early summer, when the clear current would be at its height and passage swift and easy.
units.literal: Youxian went out as Grand Secretary to supervise the Two Jiangs, expecting grain from eight provinces to finish crossing the river by early summer, riding the full rise of clear water for swift, easy floating passage.

units.zh: 培厚所部尤速達，為嘉慶以來數十年所未有，攸銛特疏陳給敘。
units.en: Peihou's section of the transport was especially fast—unmatched in decades since the Jiaqing reign—and Jiang Youxian submitted a special memorial recommending him for commendation and promotion.
units.literal: Peihou's jurisdiction was especially swift in delivery, something not seen in decades since Jiaqing; Youxian specially memorialized requesting reward and promotion for him.

units.zh: 曆三運無誤，上意方鄉用，以勞卒於通州運次。
units.en: He completed three transport cycles without a hitch just as the throne was turning toward promoting him, but he died of exhaustion at the Tongzhou transport depot.
units.literal: Through three transport cycles without error, the court was just turning toward employing him when he died of overwork at the Tongzhou transport station.

units.zh: 李象鶤，字云皋，湖南長沙人。
units.en: Li Xiangkun, whose style was Yungao, came from Changsha in Hunan.
units.literal: Li Xiangkun, style Yungao, was a native of Changsha in Hunan.

units.zh: 嘉慶十六年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。
units.en: He earned his jinshi degree in the sixteenth year of the Jiaqing reign, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.
units.literal: In the sixteenth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

units.zh: 道光二年，出為直隸宣化知府。
units.en: In the second year of the Daoguang reign he was posted as prefect of Xuanhua in Zhili.
units.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he went out as prefect of Xuanhua in Zhili.

units.zh: 歲饑，禁姦販，安屯戶，煮粥以賑，民無失所。
units.en: When famine struck, he banned hoarding and profiteering, settled military colonists, and distributed congee relief so that no one was left destitute.
units.literal: In a year of famine he forbade profiteering, settled military colonists, and gave gruel relief; the people lost no homes.

units.zh: 課士有法，一變邊郡弇陋之習。
units.en: He taught the local scholars with real method and transformed the backward customs of that frontier prefecture.
units.literal: He instructed scholars with method and altogether changed the narrow, crude habits of the border prefecture.

units.zh: 調正定，再調保定。
units.en: He was transferred first to Zhengding and then to Baoding.
units.literal: He was transferred to Zhengding, then again to Baoding.

units.zh: 蔣攸銛、那彥成先後為總督，皆倚如左右手。
units.en: Jiang Youxian and Na Yancheng served as governor-general in turn, and each relied on him as indispensable as his own two hands.
units.literal: Jiang Youxian and Na Yancheng successively served as governor-general and both relied on him as on their right and left hands.

units.zh: 象鶤持正無撓，擢通永道，調河南鹽道。
units.en: Xiangkun stood firm and would not bend; he was promoted intendant of the Tong-Yong circuit and then transferred to serve as Henan salt intendant.
units.literal: Xiangkun was upright and unbending; he was promoted intendant of Tong-Yong circuit and transferred to Henan salt intendant.

units.zh: 治漕嚴，弁丁懍懍，禁胥役藉僱剝船擾民，請潞鹽仍歸商運，民便之。
units.en: He ran the grain transport with strict discipline, kept the boat crews in awe, and stopped clerks and runners from harassing the people by extorting hired labor on the boats; he also petitioned that Lu salt be returned to merchant carriage, which greatly benefited the populace.
units.literal: He governed the grain transport strictly; boatmen were in awe; he forbade clerks and runners from using hired stripping of boats to harass the people; he requested that Lu salt again be returned to merchant transport, to the people's convenience.

units.zh: 丁父艱歸，服闋，補江西吉南贛寧道。
units.en: After mourning his father and completing the mourning period, he was appointed intendant of the Ji-Nan-Gan-Ning circuit in Jiangxi.
units.literal: He returned home on his father's death; when mourning ended he was appointed to the Ji-Nan-Gan-Ning circuit in Jiangxi.

units.zh: 轄境與粵東犬牙相錯，多伏莽，屬縣僻瘠，幾不可治，象鶤掃除積弊，境內秩然。
units.en: His circuit bordered eastern Guangdong in a tangled checkerboard of territory, with brigands lurking everywhere and remote, impoverished counties that seemed almost beyond governance; Xiangkun cleared out long-standing abuses until order prevailed throughout the region.
units.literal: His jurisdiction interlocked with eastern Guangdong like dog's teeth; there were many hidden brigands; subordinate counties were remote and poor, nearly ungovernable. Xiangkun swept away accumulated abuses and within the borders order prevailed.

units.zh: 擢江蘇按察使，署江寧布政使。
units.en: He was promoted provincial judge of Jiangsu and served as acting provincial treasurer of Jiangning.
units.literal: He was promoted Jiangsu provincial judge and acted as Jiangning provincial treasurer.

units.zh: 時陶澍為總督，賴其佐理焉。
units.en: Governor-General Tao Shu relied heavily on him to help run the province.
units.literal: At the time Tao Shu was governor-general and relied on him to assist in administration.

units.zh: 調貴州按察使。
units.en: He was transferred to serve as provincial judge of Guizhou.
units.literal: He was transferred to Guizhou provincial judge.

units.zh: 仁懷奸民為亂，株連眾，治之無枉縱。
units.en: When troublemakers in Renhuai stirred up a revolt and many were implicated, he tried the case without either executing the innocent or letting the guilty go free.
units.literal: Wicked men in Renhuai made trouble; many were implicated by association; he handled the case without wrongful execution or release.

units.zh: 擢布政使，禁漢奸盤剝苗民，多惠政。
units.en: Promoted provincial treasurer, he barred Han collaborators from exploiting the Miao and enacted many policies that benefited the people.
units.literal: He was promoted provincial treasurer, forbade Han collaborators from exploiting the Miao people, and enacted many benevolent policies.

units.zh: 二十四年，以假去職。
units.en: In the twenty-fourth year of the reign he left office on personal leave.
units.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he left office on leave.

units.zh: 洎入覲，詔以三品京堂候補。
units.en: When he later presented himself at court, he was ordered to await appointment as a third-rank capital official.
units.literal: When he came to audience, an edict appointed him to await assignment as a third-rank capital official.

units.zh: 未幾，乞歸。
units.en: Before long he petitioned to retire to his home.
units.literal: Before long he requested to retire home.

units.zh: 李宗傳，字孝曾，安徽桐城人。
units.en: Li Zongchuan, whose style was Xiaozeng, came from Tongcheng in Anhui.
units.literal: Li Zongchuan, style Xiaozeng, was a native of Tongcheng in Anhui.

units.zh: 嘉慶三年舉人。
units.en: He passed the provincial examination in the third year of the Jiaqing reign.
units.literal: In the third year of Jiaqing he passed the provincial examination.

units.zh: 授浙江上虞知縣先攝麗水、平湖、瑞安、建德、平陽，所至求民隱，鋤豪強，平反冤獄。
units.en: Appointed magistrate of Shangyu in Zhejiang, he had earlier served in acting posts at Lishui, Pinghu, Rui'an, Jiande, and Pingyang; everywhere he went he sought out the people's grievances, broke the power of local bullies, and overturned unjust verdicts.
units.literal: Appointed magistrate of Shangyu in Zhejiang, he first acted for Lishui, Pinghu, Rui'an, Jiande, and Pingyang; wherever he went he sought the people's hidden grievances, uprooted powerful bullies, and reversed wrongful cases.

units.zh: 在麗水斷積案七百餘事，捐貲河工，敘知府，擢浙江督糧道。
units.en: At Lishui he cleared more than seven hundred backlogged cases, donated his own money to river works, was recommended for promotion to prefect, and was elevated to grain intendant of Zhejiang.
units.literal: At Lishui he disposed of more than seven hundred backlog cases, donated funds for river works, was ranked for promotion to prefect, and was promoted grain intendant of Zhejiang.

units.zh: 道光三年，杭、嘉、湖三府大水，宗傳建議，浙西諸水尾閭，下由江蘇入海，必宜江、浙兩省通籌疏濬，大吏用其言，疏請合治。
units.en: When Hang, Jia, and Hu were devastated by flood in the third year of Daoguang, Zongchuan argued that the lower reaches of western Zhejiang's rivers, which discharge through Jiangsu into the sea, had to be dredged through coordinated planning by both provinces; the senior officials accepted his plan and memorialized for joint works.
units.literal: In the third year of Daoguang the three prefectures of Hang, Jia, and Hu suffered great floods. Zongchuan proposed that the tail outlets of western Zhejiang's waters, which below pass through Jiangsu to the sea, must be dredged through joint planning by the two provinces; the high officials adopted his words and memorialized requesting joint treatment.

units.zh: 坐事左遷，巡撫程含章薦之，以知府用，授湖南永州，葺濂溪書院，崇節義，勸種植。
units.en: After a demotion on disciplinary grounds, Governor Cheng Hanzhang recommended him for prefectural appointment; posted to Yongzhou in Hunan, he restored the Lianxi Academy, promoted loyalty and moral conduct, and encouraged agriculture.
units.literal: Demoted on a charge, he was recommended by Governor Cheng Hanzhang and used as prefect; he was appointed to Yongzhou in Hunan, repaired the Lianxi Academy, honored integrity and righteousness, and encouraged planting.

units.zh: 擢四川成綿龍茂道，累攝鹽道、布政使。
units.en: He was promoted intendant of the Cheng-Mian-Long-Mao circuit in Sichuan and repeatedly served in acting posts as salt intendant and provincial treasurer.
units.literal: He was promoted intendant of Cheng-Mian-Long-Mao in Sichuan and repeatedly acted as salt intendant and provincial treasurer.

units.zh: 十三年，瓘邊屬倮夷降复叛，勢甚張，總督鄂山既奏劾提督楊芳，檄宗傳往察治。
units.en: In the thirteenth year the Luo Yi on the Qian frontier, having submitted, rebelled again with great force; Governor-General E Shan had already impeached Regional Commander Yang Fang and dispatched Zongchuan to investigate and settle the matter.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year the Luo Yi of the border region under Qian submitted, rebelled again, and their power grew very great; Governor-General E Shan had already memorialized impeaching Regional Commander Yang Fang and ordered Zongchuan to go investigate and handle it.

units.zh: 宗傳上言：「四廳夷環山為巢，嗜利頑鈍，愈撫愈囂。
units.en: Zongchuan memorialized: "The Yi of the four subprefectures have their lairs in the surrounding mountains; greedy and obstinate, they grow bolder the more one tries to appease them.
units.literal: Zongchuan memorialized: "The Yi of the four subprefectures nest in the encircling mountains; greedy and stubbornly dull, the more they are pacified the more arrogant they become.

units.zh: 去年添兵設防，夷轉四出焚掠，攻壘窺城，略無忌憚。
units.en: Last year, after reinforcements were posted and defenses strengthened, the Yi instead ranged out in every direction to burn and plunder, assault stockades, and probe the cities, showing almost no restraint.
units.literal: Last year troops were added and defenses set up, yet the Yi turned to raiding in all directions, burning and plundering, attacking stockades and probing cities, with scarcely any fear.

units.zh: 雖擾一廳，實四廳安危所繫，不可姑息貽患。」
units.en: Though the trouble appears in one subprefecture, the security of all four hangs upon it; we cannot indulge them and leave a lasting menace."
units.literal: Though they trouble one subprefecture, in truth the safety of all four subprefectures is bound up with it; one cannot indulge them and leave trouble behind."

units.zh: 乃建三路進剿之策，倡助軍需，治兵選士，聲威大振。
units.en: He then proposed a three-pronged campaign, rallied contributions for the army, drilled troops and picked the best men, and his authority rose sharply.
units.literal: He then devised a plan of advance on three routes to suppress them, urged contributions of military supplies, trained troops and selected soldiers, and his prestige greatly rose.

units.zh: 三路大軍猶未至，宗傳先以計誘降十三支夷，縶之，勒還所掠人口，有業者復之，無業者給貲，縱俘歸，使諭威德。
units.en: Before the three armies even arrived, Zongchuan by stratagem induced thirteen Yi bands to surrender, seized their leaders, forced the return of captives, restored lands to those who had property, compensated those who did not, and sent prisoners home to spread word of imperial power and mercy.
units.literal: The three-route armies had not yet arrived when Zongchuan first by stratagem induced thirteen Yi bands to surrender, bound them, compelled return of seized population, restored those with livelihoods, gave funds to those without, released captives to return, and had them proclaim majesty and virtue.

units.zh: 夷猶豫未決，大軍由冷跡關逼老林巢藪，大破之於石門坎，擒斬數百，毀賊寨二百餘所，夷落悉平。
units.en: While the Yi still wavered, the main force pressed through Lengji Pass into their forest strongholds and routed them at Shimenkan, capturing or killing hundreds, destroying more than two hundred rebel camps, and pacifying every Yi settlement.
units.literal: The Yi still hesitated undecided; the great army pressed through Lengji Pass toward the old forest lairs, routed them greatly at Shimenkan, captured and beheaded several hundred, destroyed more than two hundred bandit stockades, and all Yi settlements were pacified.

units.zh: 論功最，擢山東按察使。
units.en: Rated highest for merit, he was promoted provincial judge of Shandong.
units.literal: Judged foremost in merit, he was promoted Shandong provincial judge.

units.zh: 捕大盜劉二鞍子置之法，群盜遠遁，遷湖北布政使。
units.en: He captured the notorious bandit Liu Er'anzi and executed him; the rest of the gangs fled, and he was transferred to serve as provincial treasurer of Hubei.
units.literal: He captured the great bandit Liu Er'anzi and executed him by law; bandits fled far away; he was transferred to Hubei provincial treasurer.

units.zh: 年逾七十，引疾歸。
units.en: After passing seventy, he pleaded illness and retired home.
units.literal: Past seventy years of age, he cited illness and returned home.

units.zh: 宗傳徵叛夷出奇有功，然居恆時以計取傷仁，意不自慊。
units.en: Zongchuan won distinction against the rebellious Yi through bold stratagems, yet he was uneasy at heart because his usual reliance on cunning often cut against humane conduct.
units.literal: Zongchuan in suppressing rebellious Yi achieved merit by unusual stratagems, yet in daily life he often harmed benevolence by taking through stratagem and was not at ease in his own mind.

units.zh: 嘗從同縣姚鼐遊，能文章。
units.en: He had studied under his fellow townsman Yao Nai and was himself a capable writer.
units.literal: He once associated with Yao Nai of the same county and could write essays.

units.zh: 王鳳生，字竹嶼，安徽婺源人。
units.en: Wang Fengsheng, whose style was Zhuyu, came from Wuyuan in Anhui.
units.literal: Wang Fengsheng, style Zhuyu, was a native of Wuyuan in Anhui.

units.zh: 父友亮，乾隆四十六年進士。
units.en: His father Youliang had earned his jinshi degree in the forty-sixth year of the Qianlong reign.
units.literal: His father Youliang passed the jinshi examination in the forty-sixth year of Qianlong.

units.zh: 由中書充軍機章京，累遷刑部郎中，精究法律，治獄矜慎。
units.en: Starting in the Secretariat, he served as a Grand Council clerk and rose to director in the Ministry of Punishments, where he mastered the law and tried cases with scrupulous care.
units.literal: From the Secretariat he served as a Grand Council clerk, was repeatedly promoted to director in the Ministry of Punishments, thoroughly studied law, and handled cases with cautious compassion.

units.zh: 改御史，巡城、巡漕，官至通政司副使，有清直聲。
units.en: He became a censor, took charge of city patrol and grain-transport inspection, rose to vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission, and was known for integrity and moral courage.
units.literal: He became a censor, inspected the city and inspected grain transport, rose to vice commissioner of the Communications Office, and had a reputation for purity and uprightness.

units.zh: 以詩名。
units.en: He was also celebrated as a poet.
units.literal: He was famed for poetry.

units.zh: 鳳生，嘉慶中，入貲為浙江通判，屢攝知縣事。
units.en: During the Jiaqing reign Fengsheng purchased appointment as vice-prefect of Zhejiang and repeatedly served in acting posts as county magistrate.
units.literal: Fengsheng, in the Jiaqing period, purchased office as Zhejiang vice-prefect and repeatedly acted as magistrate.

units.zh: 任蘭溪僅數月，清積案七百餘事。
units.en: In only a few months at Lanxi he cleared more than seven hundred backlogged cases.
units.literal: Serving at Lanxi for only a few months, he cleared more than seven hundred backlog cases.

units.zh: 任平湖，有民數百戶，誦經茹素，傳授邪教，鳳生憫其愚惑，開諭利害，治為首數人罪，餘釋之。
units.en: At Pinghu several hundred households were chanting scriptures, eating vegetarian fare, and spreading a heterodox sect; Fengsheng pitied their delusion, explained the consequences to them, punished only the ringleaders, and released the rest.
units.literal: At Pinghu several hundred households chanted sutras, ate vegetarian food, and transmitted heterodox teachings; Fengsheng pitied their foolish delusion, explained harms and benefits, punished several ringleaders, and released the rest.

units.zh: 補嘉興府通判。
units.en: He received a regular appointment as vice-prefect of Jiaxing.
units.literal: He was appointed vice-prefect of Jiaxing prefecture.

units.zh: 道光初，浙江清查倉庫，以鳳生總其事。
units.en: Early in the Daoguang reign, when Zhejiang undertook a general audit of granaries and storehouses, Fengsheng was placed in overall charge.
units.literal: At the beginning of Daoguang Zhejiang audited granaries and warehouses, with Fengsheng in overall charge.

units.zh: 署嘉興知府，遷玉環廳同知。
units.en: He served as acting prefect of Jiaxing and was then transferred to be subprefect of Yuhuan.
units.literal: He acted as Jiaxing prefect and was transferred subprefect of Yuhuan subprefecture.

units.zh: 會浙西大水，江、浙兩省議合治，調鳳生乍浦同知，勘水道，乃由天目山歷湖州、嘉興，沿太湖以達松江。
units.en: When western Zhejiang was hit by severe flooding and Jiangsu and Zhejiang agreed on joint works, Fengsheng was transferred to Zhapu to survey the waterways, tracing a route from Mount Tianmu through Huzhou and Jiaxing along Lake Tai to Songjiang.
units.literal: When western Zhejiang suffered great flood and the two provinces of Jiang and Zhe discussed joint treatment, Fengsheng was transferred subprefect of Zhapu to survey waterways, going from Mount Tianmu through Huzhou and Jiaxing along Tai Lake to reach Songjiang.

units.zh: 計畫甫就，事未行，值淮南高堰潰決，江南大吏疏調鳳生赴南河。
units.en: His plan was barely finished when the Gaoyan embankment on the Huainan front burst; the senior officials of Jiangnan memorialized to transfer him to the Southern River works.
units.literal: The plan was just completed but not yet carried out when the Gaoyan embankment in Huainan burst; Jiangnan high officials memorialized transferring Fengsheng to the Southern River.

units.zh: 未幾，擢河南歸德知府，濬虞城、夏邑、永城三縣溝渠。
units.en: Soon afterward he was promoted prefect of Guide in Henan, where he dredged the canals and ditches of Yucheng, Xiayi, and Yongcheng.
units.literal: Before long he was promoted prefect of Guide in Henan and dredged canals and ditches in the three counties of Yucheng, Xiayi, and Yongcheng.

units.zh: 尋擢彰衛懷道，道屬河工五廳，歲修糜費，春秋防汛，虛應故事，鳳生力矯積習，事必躬親。
units.en: He was soon promoted intendant of the Zhang-Wei-Huai circuit, where the five river offices had long squandered funds on annual repairs and seasonal flood duty in hollow observance of form; Fengsheng fought these entrenched abuses and oversaw every task himself.
units.literal: Soon he was promoted intendant of Zhang-Wei-Huai; the circuit's five river offices wasted funds on annual repairs and spring-autumn flood defense in empty compliance with routine; Fengsheng strove to correct accumulated habits and personally attended to every matter.

units.zh: 以歲修有定例，另案無定例，在任三年，力刪另案以杜弊。
units.en: Annual repairs followed fixed quotas while supplemental projects did not; during three years in office he worked hard to abolish those supplemental accounts and shut down corruption.
units.literal: Because annual repairs had fixed regulations but supplemental cases had no fixed regulations, in three years in office he strove to cut supplemental cases to stop abuses.

units.zh: 尋以疾乞歸。
units.en: Before long he petitioned to retire home on grounds of illness.
units.literal: Soon he requested to return home on account of illness.

units.zh: 九年，兩江總督蔣攸銛薦起原官，署兩淮鹽運使。
units.en: In the ninth year Governor-General Jiang Youxian of the Two Jiangs had him recalled to his former rank, and he served as acting Liang-Huai salt transport commissioner.
units.literal: In the ninth year Two-Jiangs Governor-General Jiang Youxian recommended restoring his former office; he acted as Liang-Huai salt transport commissioner.

units.zh: 鳳生以淮鹽極敝，條上十八事。
units.en: Seeing how badly the Huai salt system had decayed, Fengsheng submitted a detailed program of eighteen reforms.
units.literal: Fengsheng, because Huai salt was extremely decayed, submitted in articles eighteen items.

units.zh: 攸銛採其議，改灶鹽，節浮費，濬河道，增屯船，緝場私、鄰私之出入，禁江船、漕船之夾帶，及清查庫款，督運淮北諸條，疏陳待施行，會詔捕鹽梟巨魁黃玉林，鳳生計招出首，責緝私贖罪。
units.en: Jiang Youxian adopted his proposals—reforming furnace salt, cutting waste, dredging waterways, adding transport vessels, cracking down on field and cross-border smuggling, banning contraband on river and grain boats, auditing treasury funds, and tightening north-of-Huai transport—and memorialized the package for implementation. When the throne ordered the capture of the salt-smuggling kingpin Huang Yulin, Fengsheng devised a plan to induce the chief culprit to surrender and required him to hunt smugglers in exchange for clemency.
units.literal: Youxian adopted his proposals: reforming furnace salt, cutting superfluous expenses, dredging river channels, increasing transport boats, seizing field smuggling and neighboring smuggling in and out, forbidding river boats and grain boats from carrying contraband, and auditing treasury funds, supervising transport north of the Huai and other items; memorialized awaiting implementation. When an edict ordered capture of the great salt smuggling chief Huang Yulin, Fengsheng planned to induce the chief culprit to come forward and charged him to seize smugglers to redeem guilt.

units.zh: 攸銛已入告，旋因告訐置之獄，又得玉林所寄其黨私書，意反复，密疏請處以重法。
units.en: Jiang Youxian had already reported the surrender to the throne, but Yulin was soon jailed after an informer's accusation; when letters from Yulin to his gang were found, Jiang took this as proof of double-dealing and secretly memorialized for the severest penalty.
units.literal: Youxian had already reported to the throne; soon because of denunciation Yulin was put in prison; he also obtained private letters Yulin sent his gang, thought him double-minded, and in a secret memorial requested heavy punishment.

units.zh: 上以前後歧異，譴攸銛，鳳生亦降調。
units.en: The emperor, seeing the contradiction between the two accounts, censured Jiang Youxian and demoted Fengsheng as well.
units.literal: The emperor, because of the contradiction before and after, reprimanded Youxian and Fengsheng was also demoted.

units.zh: 陶澍繼督兩江，與尚書王鼎、侍郎寶興會籌鹽法，合疏留鳳生襄議，於是大有興革，略與鳳生初議相出入；
units.en: Tao Shu succeeded as governor-general of the Two Jiangs and, with Minister Wang Ding and Vice Minister Bao Xing, worked out salt reforms; they jointly memorialized to keep Fengsheng to help draft the plan, and the resulting overhaul largely followed, though not entirely, his original proposals;
units.literal: Tao Shu succeeded as governor of the Two Jiangs; with Minister Wang Ding and Vice Minister Bao Xing he jointly planned salt law, jointly memorialized to retain Fengsheng to assist in deliberation; thereupon great innovations and abolitions were made, roughly agreeing and differing with Fengsheng's original proposals;

units.zh: 又奏以鳳生察湖廣銷引，勘議淮北改票事，鳳生雖去官，仍與鹽事終始。
units.en: They also had him inspect salt distribution in Huguang and study north-of-Huai ticket reform; though out of office, Fengsheng remained involved in salt policy from start to finish.
units.literal: They also memorialized appointing Fengsheng to inspect Huguang sales quotas and survey north-of-Huai ticket reform; though Fengsheng had left office, he still was involved in salt affairs from beginning to end.

units.zh: 十二年，湖北大潦，總督盧坤疏留鳳生治江、漢堤工，袤亙數百里，半載告竣，秋水至，新堤有潰者，鳳生引咎乞疾歸。
units.en: In the twelfth year, after severe flooding in Hubei, Governor Lu Kun kept Fengsheng to repair hundreds of li of Yangtze and Han dikes; the work was declared finished in half a year, but when the autumn floods came some new embankments gave way, and Fengsheng took the blame and retired on grounds of illness.
units.literal: In the twelfth year Hubei suffered great flood; Governor Lu Kun memorialized retaining Fengsheng to manage Yangtze and Han embankment works stretching hundreds of li; in half a year it was reported complete; when autumn water came, new dikes had breaches; Fengsheng took blame and requested to return home on illness.

units.zh: 尋淮北票鹽大暢，陶澍以鳳生首議功上聞，促之出，未行而卒。
units.en: Soon ticket salt north of the Huai was thriving; Tao Shu reported Fengsheng's pioneering role to the throne and urged him to return to service, but he died before he could set out.
units.literal: Soon north-of-Huai ticket salt flowed greatly; Tao Shu reported Fengsheng's merit as first proposer to the throne and urged him to come out; before he went he died.

units.zh: 鳳生以仕為學，尤篤好圖誌，成浙西水利圖說備考、河北采風錄、江淮河運圖、漢江紀程、江漢宣防備考、淮南北場河運鹽走私道路圖，每吏一方，必能指畫其形勢，與所宜興革。
units.en: Fengsheng treated public service as his school of learning and was devoted to maps and local gazetteers, producing works such as Investigative Notes on Western Zhejiang Waterworks, Hebei Customs Record, Jiang-Huai River Transport Atlas, Han River Journey, Jiang-Han Flood-Control Notes, and maps of salt-smuggling routes on the Huai; in every post he could sketch the terrain and spell out what ought to be changed.
units.literal: Fengsheng took office as study and especially loved maps and gazetteers, completing such works as Investigative Notes on Western Zhejiang Water Conservancy Maps, Hebei Customs Record, Jiang-Huai River Transport Map, Han River Journey, Jiang-Han Flood Defense Investigative Notes, and Maps of Salt Smuggling Routes on North and South Huai River Transport; wherever he served as official he could point out terrain and what should be promoted or reformed.

units.zh: 四方大吏爭相疏調，少竟其用，惟治淮鹽尤為陶澍所倚藉焉。
units.en: Officials everywhere competed to have him transferred to their jurisdictions, yet few made full use of his talents; Tao Shu relied on him above all for reforming Huai salt.
units.literal: High officials in all directions competed to memorialize transferring him; few fully used his talents; only in governing Huai salt was he especially relied on by Tao Shu.

units.zh: 黃冕，字服週，湖南長沙人。
units.en: Huang Mian, whose style was Fuzhou, came from Changsha in Hunan.
units.literal: Huang Mian, style Fuzhou, was a native of Changsha in Hunan.

units.zh: 年二十，官兩淮鹽大使，治淮、揚賑有聲。
units.en: At twenty he was appointed Liang-Huai salt commissioner and won renown for famine relief in the Huai-Yang region.
units.literal: At age twenty he served as Liang-Huai salt distribution commissioner and was famed for relief work in Huai and Yang.

units.zh: 初行海運，巡撫陶澍使赴上海集沙船與議，盡得要領，授江都知縣。
units.en: When sea transport was first introduced, Governor Tao Shu sent him to Shanghai to negotiate with the sand-shipping fleets; having mastered every detail, he was appointed magistrate of Jiangdu.
units.literal: When sea transport was first instituted, Governor Tao Shu sent him to Shanghai to gather sand boats for consultation; he grasped all essentials and was appointed magistrate of Jiangdu.

units.zh: 曆元和、上海，署太倉州，擢蘇州府同知，晉秩知府，署常州、鎮江，有大興作，大吏悉倚以辦。
units.en: He served in Yuanhe and Shanghai, acted as prefect of Taicang, was promoted vice-prefect of Suzhou and then to prefect, and held acting posts at Changzhou and Zhenjiang; whenever major projects arose, the senior officials relied on him to carry them out.
units.literal: He served at Yuanhe and Shanghai, acted at Taicang prefecture, was promoted Suzhou vice-prefect, advanced in rank to prefect, acted at Changzhou and Zhenjiang; when great works arose, high officials all relied on him to handle them.

units.zh: 疏治劉河海口，上海蒲匯塘，常州芙蓉江、孟河，冕皆躬任之。
units.en: He personally oversaw dredging at the mouth of the Liu River, Shanghai's Puhui Pond, and Changzhou's Furong and Meng rivers.
units.literal: Dredging the mouth of the Liu River, Shanghai's Puhui Pond, Changzhou's Furong River and Meng River—Mian personally took charge of all.

units.zh: 海疆兵事起，從總督裕謙赴浙江。
units.en: When war broke out on the coast, he accompanied Governor Yuqian to Zhejiang.
units.literal: When coastal military affairs arose, he followed Governor Yuqian to Zhejiang.

units.zh: 裕謙死難，冕牽連遣戍伊犁，既而林則徐亦至戍，議興屯田，冕佐治水利有功，赦還。
units.en: After Yuqian died in battle, Huang was implicated and exiled to Yili; when Lin Zexu was sent to the same frontier and colonization was proposed, Huang helped manage the irrigation works with distinction and was eventually pardoned and allowed to return.
units.literal: Yuqian died in the line of duty; Mian was implicated and sent in exile to Yili; soon Lin Zexu also arrived in exile; when colonization farming was proposed, Mian assisted in managing waterworks with merit and was pardoned and returned.

units.zh: 江蘇巡撫陸建瀛復調冕治海運，革漕費，歲省銀數十萬，為忌者所中，劾罷歸。
units.en: Jiangsu Governor Lu Jianying recalled him to run the sea transport, abolished extraneous grain-shipping charges, and saved several hundred thousand taels a year; jealous rivals brought him down by impeachment and he returned home.
units.literal: Jiangsu Governor Lu Jianying again transferred Mian to manage sea transport, abolished grain transport fees, saving several hundred thousand taels yearly; he was struck by jealous enemies, impeached and dismissed to return home.

units.zh: 咸豐初，粵匪圍長沙，冕建守禦策。
units.en: Early in the Xianfeng reign, when the Taiping rebels besieged Changsha, Huang drew up the city's defense plans.
units.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng the Cantonese rebels besieged Changsha; Mian devised defense plans.

units.zh: 及曾國籓治兵討賊，冕創釐稅，興茶鹽之利，軍餉取給焉。
units.en: When Zeng Guofan raised an army against the rebels, Huang instituted the lijin transit tax and developed tea and salt revenues to fund the troops.
units.literal: When Zeng Guofan raised troops to suppress rebels, Mian created the lijin tax and promoted tea and salt profits; military funds were supplied from them.

units.zh: 又開東征局，專餉曾國籓一軍。
units.en: He also set up an Eastern Campaign Bureau devoted solely to provisioning Zeng Guofan's forces.
units.literal: He also opened an Eastern Campaign Bureau to supply only Zeng Guofan's army.

units.zh: 起授江西吉安知府，復以事劾免歸，仍以餉事自任，湘軍賴以成功。
units.en: Recalled to serve as prefect of Ji'an in Jiangxi, he was impeached and sent home again, yet still took charge of supply work on his own; the Hunan army depended on him for its success.
units.literal: Recalled and appointed prefect of Ji'an in Jiangxi, he was again impeached and dismissed home, yet still took supply affairs upon himself; the Hunan army relied on this for success.

units.zh: 尋授雲南迤西道，辭病不赴，卒於家。
units.en: Soon afterward he was appointed intendant of western Yunnan, but pleaded illness and declined; he died at home.
units.literal: Soon appointed intendant of Yixi in Yunnan, he declined on illness and did not go; he died at home.

units.zh: 冕仕宦初為陶澍、林則徐所知，晚在籍為駱秉章所倚任。
units.en: Early in his career he won the notice of Tao Shu and Lin Zexu; in later years, while living at home, he was entrusted by Luo Bingzhang.
units.literal: In office Mian was first known to Tao Shu and Lin Zexu; late while at home he was relied on by Luo Bingzhang.

units.zh: 時稱其幹濟，被謗亦甚云。
units.en: Contemporaries praised his practical ability, yet he was also said to have been the target of fierce slander.
units.literal: At the time he was praised for practical ability, and it was also said that he was greatly slandered.

units.zh: 俞德淵，字陶泉，甘肅平羅人。
units.en: Yu Deyuan, whose style was Taoquan, came from Pingluo in Gansu.
units.literal: Yu Deyuan, style Taoquan, was a native of Pingluo in Gansu.

units.zh: 嘉慶二十二年進士，選庶吉士，散館授江蘇荊溪知縣。
units.en: He earned his jinshi degree in the twenty-second year of the Jiaqing reign, entered the Hanlin Academy, and upon completing his term there was appointed magistrate of Jingxi in Jiangsu.
units.literal: In the twenty-second year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and upon leaving the academy was appointed magistrate of Jingxi in Jiangsu.

units.zh: 始至，遮訴者百十輩，逾年，前訴者又易名來控，一見即識之，群驚為神。
units.en: On his arrival more than a hundred plaintiffs waylaid him; a year later former litigants returned under false names, yet he recognized them at once, and onlookers were astonished as if he were superhuman.
units.literal: When he first arrived, over a hundred litigants blocked his path; after a year former litigants came to accuse again under changed names; at one glance he recognized them, and the crowd marveled as at a god.

units.zh: 調長洲，甚得民心。
units.en: Transferred to Changzhou, he won the deep affection of the people.
units.literal: Transferred to Changzhou, he greatly won the people's hearts.

units.zh: 遷蘇州督糧同知。
units.en: He was promoted to grain supervisor vice-prefect of Suzhou.
units.literal: He was promoted grain supervisor vice-prefect of Suzhou.

units.zh: 道光六年，初行海運，以德淵董其役，章程皆出手定，以憂去。
units.en: In the sixth year of Daoguang, when sea transport was first introduced, Deyuan was placed in overall charge and drafted every regulation himself, but left office to mourn a parent.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Daoguang, when sea transport was first instituted, Deyuan was placed in charge; all regulations were drawn by his own hand; he left on account of mourning.

units.zh: 八年，服闋，擢常州知府，調江寧。
units.en: In the eighth year, after mourning, he was promoted prefect of Changzhou and transferred to Jiangning.
units.literal: In the eighth year, when mourning ended, he was promoted prefect of Changzhou and transferred to Jiangning.

units.zh: 十年，宣宗以兩淮鹽法大壞，授陶澍為兩江總督，命尚書王鼎、侍郎寶興赴江南會議改革。
units.en: In the tenth year, seeing how badly the Liang-Huai salt system had decayed, the Xuanzong Emperor appointed Tao Shu governor-general of the Two Jiangs and sent Minister Wang Ding and Vice Minister Bao Xing to Jiangnan to plan reforms.
units.literal: In the tenth year the Xuanzong Emperor, because Liang-Huai salt law was greatly corrupted, appointed Tao Shu Two-Jiangs governor-general and ordered Minister Wang Ding and Vice Minister Bao Xing to go to Jiangnan to confer on reform.

units.zh: 時議者多主罷官商鹽，歸場灶科稅，以德淵有心計，使與議。
units.en: Most reformers then favored abolishing the official-merchant salt system and taxing production at the salt fields and furnaces; because Deyuan was known for shrewd planning, he was brought into the discussions.
units.literal: At the time most debaters favored abolishing official-merchant salt and returning taxation to the salt fields and furnaces; because Deyuan had resourceful plans, he was made to join the deliberation.

units.zh: 德淵具議數千言，略謂：「鹽歸場灶，其法有三：一曰歸灶丁按䥕起科，然其中有難行者三：一在灶丁之逋欠，一在䥕鑊之私煎，一在災祲之藉口；
units.en: Deyuan submitted a memorial several thousand characters long, arguing in essence: "Returning salt revenue to the fields and furnaces admits three approaches. The first is to levy on furnace workers by salt pan, but three difficulties stand in the way: arrears among the workers, illicit private boiling, and disasters invoked as excuses;
units.literal: Deyuan submitted a memorial of several thousand characters, saying in summary: "If salt returns to the fields and furnaces, there are three methods: first, levy on furnace workers by salt pan; yet within this there are three difficulties: first in furnace workers' arrears, second in private boiling at salt vats, third in disasters as pretext;

units.zh: 二曰歸場官給單收稅，難行者亦有三：一在額數之難定，一在稽查之難週，一在官吏之難恃；
units.en: The second is for field officials to issue receipts and collect tax directly, but here too there are three difficulties: setting fixed quotas, conducting thorough inspections, and relying on local officials;
units.literal: second, field officials issue receipts and collect tax; here too there are three difficulties: first in fixing quotas, second in thorough inspection, third in relying on officials;

units.zh: 三曰歸場商認䥕納課，難行者亦有三：一在疲商之鑽充，一在殷戶之規避，一在垣外之私售。
units.en: The third is for licensed merchants at the fields to contract for pans and pay duty, but again three difficulties arise: bankrupt merchants muscling in, wealthy households evading registration, and illicit sales beyond the salt yards;
units.literal: third, field merchants contract for salt pans and pay duty; here too there are three difficulties: first in worn-out merchants forcing their way in, second in wealthy households evading, third in private sales outside the salt yards;

units.zh: 以上三法，共有九難。
units.en: Taken together, these three schemes present nine serious difficulties.
units.literal: Among the three methods above, there are nine difficulties in all.

units.zh: 如就三者兼權之，則招商認䥕，猶為此善於彼。
units.en: If one weighs all three together, inviting merchants to contract for salt pans is still the least bad option.
units.literal: If one weighs all three together, then inviting merchants to contract for salt pans is still better than the others.

units.zh: 苟得其人，或可講求盡善。
units.en: With the right men in charge, it might even be made to work tolerably well.
units.literal: If the right men are obtained, perhaps one can seek to make it as perfect as possible.

units.zh: 顧事關圖始，果欲行之，則宜先定章程。
units.en: Yet this is a matter of founding an entirely new system; if it is truly to be attempted, regulations must be settled first.
units.literal: But the matter concerns founding a new system; if one truly wishes to carry it out, one should first fix regulations.

units.zh: 清灶僉商、改官易制諸事，非三年不能就緒。
units.en: Clearing the furnaces, enrolling merchants, replacing officials, and changing institutions cannot be completed in less than three years.
units.literal: Clearing furnaces, enrolling merchants, changing officials and altering institutions—without three years it cannot be brought to readiness.

units.zh: 此三年中，額課未可長懸也，場鹽未可停售也，各岸食鹽未可久缺也。
units.en: During those three years, quota revenue cannot be left in suspense, salt from the fields cannot stop being sold, and the consuming provinces cannot long go without supply.
units.literal: Within these three years, quota revenue cannot long be suspended, field salt cannot stop being sold, and salt for consumption at the various banks cannot long be lacking.

units.zh: 新舊接替之時，非熟思審處，何能變通盡利乎？
units.en: At the moment of transition from old to new, how can the change be managed for full benefit without careful, deliberate planning?
units.literal: At the time of old and new handover, without mature thought and careful handling, how can one adapt flexibly and exhaust the benefits?

units.zh: 向來捆鹽之夫，淮北永豐有萬餘人，淮南老虎頸不下數万人，皆無賴遊民以此為事業。
units.en: The men who bundled salt for transport numbered more than ten thousand at Yongfeng north of the Huai and tens of thousands at Laohujing south of the Huai—all rootless drifters who lived by that trade alone.
units.literal: Formerly salt-bundling laborers numbered over ten thousand at Yongfeng north of the Huai and no fewer than tens of thousands at Laohujing south of the Huai—all idle wanderers who made this their livelihood.

units.zh: 一旦失所，此數万眾將安往？
units.en: If they lose their livelihood overnight, where are these tens of thousands to go?
units.literal: Once they lose their livelihood, where will these tens of thousands go?

units.zh: 其患又不止私梟拒捕已也。」
units.en: The danger would extend far beyond smugglers resisting arrest."
units.literal: The harm is not limited to smugglers resisting arrest."

units.zh: 議上，陶澍深然之，乃與朝使定議，不歸場灶，仍用官商如故；
units.en: When the memorial reached him, Tao Shu strongly agreed; he and the imperial commissioners then decided not to return revenue to the fields and furnaces but to keep the official-merchant system as before;
units.literal: When the memorial went up, Tao Shu deeply approved; thereupon with the court envoys he fixed policy not to return to fields and furnaces but to use official merchants as before;

units.zh: 惟奏罷鹽政，裁浮費，減窩價，凡積弊皆除之。
units.en: they memorialized instead to abolish the salt commissioner, cut waste, reduce nest prices, and sweep away every entrenched abuse.
units.literal: only memorializing to abolish the salt commissioner, cut superfluous expenses, reduce nest prices, and remove all accumulated abuses.

units.zh: 薦德淵超擢兩淮鹽運使。
units.en: He recommended Deyuan for exceptional promotion to Liang-Huai salt transport commissioner.
units.literal: He recommended Deyuan for exceptional promotion to Liang-Huai salt transport commissioner.

units.zh: 德淵精會計，又知人善任。
units.en: Deyuan was a master of accounts and knew how to choose and deploy the right men.
units.literal: Deyuan was expert in accounting and also knew men and employed them well.

units.zh: 諸滯岸商憚往運，改以官督辦，千里行鹽，稽覈價用，瑣屑悉當。
units.en: When merchants at slow-selling depots refused to transport salt, he switched to official supervision; over thousand-li hauls he audited prices and costs down to the smallest item.
units.literal: Merchants at stagnant banks feared to transport; it was changed to official supervision; transporting salt a thousand li, checking prices and expenses, every trifle was handled rightly.

units.zh: 每運恆有餘利，盡以充庫，無私取。
units.en: Every shipment yielded a surplus, all of which went into the public treasury; he took nothing for himself.
units.literal: Each transport always had surplus profit, all paid into the treasury, with no private taking.

units.zh: 兩淮本脂膏地，運使多以財結權貴及四方遊客，餘贍給寒畯，取聲譽，皆出商貲。
units.en: The Two Huai were a wealthy region; transport commissioners typically used merchant money to court powerful nobles and visiting guests, then distributed the rest to poor scholars for reputation.
units.literal: The Two Huai were originally a rich region; transport commissioners often used wealth to bind powerful nobles and travelers from all directions, the remainder supporting poor scholars for reputation—all from merchant funds.

units.zh: 德淵謹守筦鑰，失望者眾，言者時相攻訐，不顧也。
units.en: Deyuan kept a tight grip on the treasury keys; many were disappointed, and critics assailed him constantly, but he paid no attention.
units.literal: Deyuan strictly guarded the keys; many were disappointed; critics often attacked one another, but he paid no heed.

units.zh: 在任五年，力崇節儉，妻子常衣布素，揚州華侈之俗為之一變。
units.en: During five years in office he promoted frugality with all his strength; his wife and children wore only plain cloth, and Yangzhou's extravagant ways were transformed.
units.literal: In five years in office he vigorously promoted frugality; wife and children constantly wore plain cloth; Yangzhou's luxurious customs were thereby changed.

units.zh: 尚書黃鉞子中民為場大使，欲得美職，德淵曰：「美職以待有功，中民無功不可得。」
units.en: Minister Huang Yue's son Zhongmin, a field commissioner, sought a desirable post; Deyuan replied: "Desirable posts are reserved for men of merit; Zhongmin has none and cannot have one."
units.literal: Minister Huang Yue's son Zhongmin was a field commissioner and wanted a fine post; Deyuan said: "Fine posts await those with merit; Zhongmin without merit cannot obtain one."

units.zh: 堅不與。
units.en: He refused firmly.
units.literal: He firmly would not grant it.

units.zh: 陶澍益賢之，薦其才可大用，以循良久在鹽官可惜，上亦嘉之，未及擢用而卒。
units.en: Tao Shu admired him all the more, recommended him for higher office, and lamented that a man of such talent should linger so long in the salt administration; the emperor praised him too, but he died before he could be promoted.
units.literal: Tao Shu increasingly esteemed him, recommended his talent for great employment, saying it was a pity that one so long in salt office remained only a circuit intendant; the emperor also praised him, but before promotion he died.

units.zh: 姚瑩，字石甫，安徽桐城人。
units.en: Yao Ying, whose style was Shipu, came from Tongcheng in Anhui.
units.literal: Yao Ying, style Shipu, was a native of Tongcheng in Anhui.

units.zh: 嘉慶十三年進士，授福建平和知縣。
units.en: He earned his jinshi degree in the thirteenth year of the Jiaqing reign and was appointed magistrate of Pinghe in Fujian.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Pinghe in Fujian.

units.zh: 調龍溪，俗健悍，械鬥仇殺無虛日。
units.en: Transferred to Longxi, where the people were fierce and armed feuds and revenge killings occurred almost daily.
units.literal: Transferred to Longxi, where customs were fierce and sturdy, armed fights and vengeance killings occurred not a day without.

units.zh: 瑩擒巨惡立斃之，收豪猾為用，予以自新。
units.en: Yao seized the worst offenders and executed them on the spot, then enlisted local strongmen and gave them a chance to reform.
units.literal: Ying seized great evildoers and immediately executed them, enrolled fierce ruffians for use, and gave them chance to reform.

units.zh: 親巡問疾苦，使侵奪者各還舊業，誓解仇讎。
units.en: He toured in person to hear the people's grievances, restored seized property, and had feuding parties swear to end their vendettas.
units.literal: He personally toured asking about hardships, made those who had seized property each return to old occupations, and had them swear to end feuds.

units.zh: 擇強力者為家長，約束族眾，籍壯丁為鄉勇，逐捕盜賊，有犯，責家長縛送。
units.en: He appointed strong men as clan heads to keep their kin in order, enrolled able-bodied men as village militia to hunt bandits, and held clan heads responsible for binding and delivering any offender.
units.literal: He chose strong men as clan heads to restrain their kin, registered stalwart males as village braves to pursue bandits, and when there were offenders charged the clan heads to bind and send them.

units.zh: 械鬥平，盜賊亦戢，治行為閩中第一。
units.en: Armed feuds subsided, banditry was curbed, and his record of governance ranked first in Fujian.
units.literal: Armed fights were pacified and bandits also restrained; his administration was first in Fujian.

units.zh: 調台灣，署海防同知、噶瑪蘭同知，坐事落職。
units.en: Transferred to Taiwan, he served as acting coastal defense vice-prefect and Gamlan vice-prefect, but was dismissed on disciplinary grounds.
units.literal: Transferred to Taiwan, he acted as coastal defense vice-prefect and Gamlan vice-prefect, and was dismissed on a charge.

units.zh: 尋以噶瑪蘭獲盜功，复官。
units.en: Soon afterward he was restored to office for capturing bandits at Gamlan.
units.literal: Soon on merit of capturing bandits at Gamlan he was restored to office.

units.zh: 父憂歸，服闋，改發江蘇，歷金壇、元和、武進。
units.en: After mourning his father he was reassigned to Jiangsu, serving successively at Jintan, Yuanhe, and Wujin.
units.literal: He returned home on his father's death; when mourning ended he was reassigned to Jiangsu, serving at Jintan, Yuanhe, and Wujin.

units.zh: 遷高郵知州，擢兩淮監掣同知，護鹽運使。
units.en: He was promoted prefect of Gaoyou, then elevated to Liang-Huai salt inspection vice-prefect and served as acting salt transport commissioner.
units.literal: He was promoted prefect of Gaoyou, elevated Liang-Huai salt inspection vice-prefect, and acted as salt transport commissioner.

units.zh: 先後疆吏趙慎畛、陶澍、林則徐皆薦其可大用。
units.en: Frontier governors Zhao Shenque, Tao Shu, and Lin Zexu in turn recommended him for high office.
units.literal: Successive frontier officials Zhao Shenque, Tao Shu, and Lin Zexu all recommended him as fit for great employment.

units.zh: 道光十年，特擢台灣道。
units.en: In the tenth year of Daoguang he received a special promotion to Taiwan circuit intendant.
units.literal: In the tenth year of Daoguang he was specially promoted Taiwan circuit intendant.

units.zh: 及海疆戒嚴，瑩與總兵達洪阿預為戰守計。
units.en: When the coast was placed on military alert, Yao and Regional Commander Da Hong'a drew up plans for defense in advance.
units.literal: When the coast was placed on alert, Ying and Regional Commander Da Hong'a beforehand made plans for war and defense.

units.zh: 達洪阿性剛，與同官鮮合，瑩推誠相接，一日謁謝曰：「武人不學，為子所容久矣，自今聽子而行。」
units.en: Da Hong'a was stubborn and rarely got on with his colleagues; Yao treated him with open sincerity until one day Da called to say: "We soldiers are unlettered men; you have borne with me long enough—from now on I shall follow your lead."
units.literal: Da Hong'a was by nature stubborn and rarely agreed with fellow officials; Ying met him with sincere openness; one day he called to thank him, saying: "We military men are unlearned; I have long been tolerated by you; from today I will heed you in action."

units.zh: 二十一年秋，英兵兩犯雞籠海口，明年正月，又犯大安港。
units.en: That autumn British forces twice attacked Keelung, and in the first month of the following year they struck Da'an harbor as well.
units.literal: In autumn of the twenty-first year British troops twice attacked Keelung harbor; in the first month of the next year they again attacked Da'an harbor.

units.zh: 瑩設方略，與達洪阿督兵連卻之，大有斬獲，收前所失寧波、廈門砲械甚多。
units.en: Yao devised the strategy; working with Da Hong'a he drove the enemy back again and again with heavy casualties inflicted on them, and recovered much of the artillery lost earlier at Ningbo and Xiamen.
units.literal: Ying devised strategy; with Da Hong'a he directed troops to repel them repeatedly with great kills and captures, recovering much artillery previously lost at Ningbo and Xiamen.

units.zh: 敵構奸民煽亂，海寇亦竊發，皆即捕戮，一方屹然，詔嘉獎，加二品銜，予雲騎尉世職。
units.en: When the enemy incited collaborators and sea bandits rose in secret, Yao had them seized and executed at once; the region held firm; the court commended him, raised him to second rank, and granted a hereditary Cloud Cavalry Captain title.
units.literal: The enemy incited traitorous people to stir rebellion; sea bandits also rose in secret—all were immediately captured and executed; the region stood firm; an edict praised them; he was given second-rank rank and a hereditary Cloud Cavalry Captain title.

units.zh: 洎江寧議款求息事，遂有台灣鎮道冒功之獄。
units.en: When peace talks at Jiangning sought to end the war, a case arose accusing the Taiwan commander and intendant of falsely claiming credit.
units.literal: When at Jiangning a treaty was negotiated seeking to end the affair, there arose the case of Taiwan commander and intendant falsely claiming merit.

units.zh: 故事，台灣以懸隔海外，加兵備道按察使銜，得與鎮臣專奏事。
units.en: By precedent, because Taiwan lay far overseas, its military defense intendant held provincial judge rank and could memorialize the throne jointly with the regional commander on his own authority.
units.literal: By precedent, because Taiwan was separated overseas, the military defense intendant was given provincial judge rank and could with the commander memorialize matters separately.

units.zh: 雞籠、大安之捷，飛章入告，總督怡良心不平。
units.en: Victories at Keelung and Da'an were reported by urgent memorial, to the deep displeasure of Governor Yi Liang.
units.literal: Victories at Keelung and Da'an were reported by urgent memorial; Governor Yi Liang was displeased at heart.

units.zh: 英兵留駐鼓浪嶼，前獲俘欲解內地，勢不能達，奏請便宜誅之，以絕內患，已報可，怡良仍令解省。
units.en: British troops remained on Gulangyu Island; earlier prisoners could not be sent inland, so a memorial requested discretionary execution to forestall trouble; the throne had approved, yet Yi Liang still ordered the prisoners sent to the provincial capital.
units.literal: British troops remained at Gulangyu; captives taken earlier were to be sent inland but could not reach there; memorial requested discretionary execution to cut off internal trouble; approval was already given, yet Yi Liang still ordered them sent to the provincial capital.

units.zh: 瑩與達洪阿謀曰：「大府意欲市德，藉以退鼓浪嶼之兵。
units.en: Yao and Da Hong'a agreed: "The governor wants to curry favor and use the prisoners to get the British off Gulangyu.
units.literal: Ying and Da Hong'a consulted, saying: "The governor intends to buy favor and thereby get the Gulangyu troops to withdraw.

units.zh: 兵不可退，徒示弱，不如殺之！」
units.en: The troops will not withdraw; this only shows weakness—we should kill the prisoners instead!"
units.literal: The troops cannot withdraw; it only shows weakness—better to kill them!"

units.zh: 怡良愈怒，諸帥並忌之。
units.en: Yi Liang was furious, and the senior commanders all turned against them.
units.literal: Yi Liang grew angrier; the various commanders all resented them.

units.zh: 款議既成，交還敵俘，以妄殺被劾，逮問。
units.en: After the treaty was signed and enemy prisoners were to be returned, they were impeached for unlawful execution and taken into custody.
units.literal: Once the treaty was concluded and enemy captives were to be returned, they were impeached for wrongful killing and arrested for questioning.

units.zh: 瑩與達洪阿約，義不與俘虜質，即自引咎。
units.en: Yao and Da Hong'a had agreed that they would not use prisoners as bargaining chips and at once accepted full responsibility.
units.literal: Ying and Da Hong'a agreed that on principle they would not bargain with captives and immediately took blame upon themselves.

units.zh: 宣宗心知台灣功，入獄六日，特旨以同知直隸州知州發往四川效用，至則復為總督寶興所忌。
units.en: The Xuanzong Emperor knew the true worth of the Taiwan victories; after six days in prison a special edict sent him to Sichuan as a subprefect and department magistrate to redeem himself, but there Governor Bao Xing turned against him again.
units.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor knew in his heart of Taiwan's merit; after six days in prison a special edict sent him as subprefect and Zhili department magistrate to Sichuan for service; on arrival he was again resented by Governor Bao Xing.

units.zh: 會西藏兩呼圖克圖相爭，檄往平之。
units.en: When two Tibetan hutuktus fell into conflict, he was ordered by dispatch to go and settle the dispute.
units.literal: When two hutuktus in Tibet quarreled, he was ordered by dispatch to go pacify them.

units.zh: 瑩謂：「夷人難以德化。
units.en: Yao objected: "Barbarians cannot be won over by moral suasion alone.
units.literal: Ying said: "Barbarians are hard to transform by virtue.

units.zh: 失職下僚，孑身往，徒損國威。」
units.en: A disgraced junior official going alone would only damage the nation's prestige."
units.literal: A dismissed subordinate official going alone would only harm national prestige."

units.zh: 不聽。
units.en: His advice was ignored.
units.literal: He was not heeded.

units.zh: 及至乍雅，果不得要領而返。
units.en: When he reached Zhaya, he failed to achieve anything and returned empty-handed, as he had predicted.
units.literal: When he reached Zhaya, as expected he obtained no essentials and returned.

units.zh: 總督劾其畏難規避，責再往。
units.en: The governor impeached him for shirking a difficult assignment and ordered him to go again.
units.literal: The governor impeached him for fearing difficulty and evading duty and ordered him to go again.

units.zh: 事竣，補蓬州。
units.en: When the mission ended, he was appointed magistrate of Pengzhou.
units.literal: When the affair was concluded, he was appointed to Pengzhou.

units.zh: 在州二年，引疾歸。
units.en: After two years in office he pleaded illness and retired home.
units.literal: In the prefecture two years, he cited illness and returned home.

units.zh: 文宗即位，黜大學士穆彰阿，詔宣示中外，並及瑩與達洪阿被陷狀，於是復起用，授湖北武昌鹽法道，未行，擢廣西按察使，命參大學士賽尚阿軍事。
units.en: When the Wenzong Emperor came to the throne, Grand Secretary Mujangga was dismissed and an edict to the empire also cleared Yao and Da Hong'a of the false charges against them; Yao was then restored, appointed salt law intendant at Wuchang in Hubei, and before he could take up that post was promoted provincial judge of Guangxi and ordered to join Grand Secretary Saišangga's staff.
units.literal: When the Wenzong Emperor ascended, Grand Secretary Mujangga was dismissed; an edict announced to inner and outer courts also covered how Ying and Da Hong'a had been framed; thereupon he was restored, appointed Hubei Wuchang salt law intendant, before departing was promoted Guangxi provincial judge, and ordered to join Grand Secretary Saišangga's military affairs.

units.zh: 時廣西寇漸熾，諸將不合，師久無功。
units.en: Rebels in Guangxi were growing stronger, the generals could not cooperate, and the campaign had dragged on without success.
units.literal: At the time rebels in Guangxi gradually grew fierce; generals did not cooperate; the army long had no success.

units.zh: 瑩至，任為翼長。
units.en: When Yao arrived, he was made wing commander of the staff.
units.literal: When Ying arrived, he was appointed wing commander.

units.zh: 大軍圍賊紫金山，瑩言流賊如水，必環攻以斷其逸，不聽，賊遂竄永安。
units.en: When the main force besieged the rebels on Purple Gold Mountain, Yao argued that roving bandits were like water and must be encircled completely to cut off escape; his advice was ignored, and the rebels broke out toward Yong'an.
units.literal: The great army besieged rebels at Purple Gold Mountain; Ying said roaming bandits are like water and one must encircle and attack to cut off their escape; he was not heeded, and the rebels fled to Yong'an.

units.zh: 又上書請斬僨事將，復不聽。
units.en: He memorialized again asking that incompetent generals be executed; again he was ignored.
units.literal: He again memorialized requesting execution of incompetent generals; again he was not heeded.

units.zh: 永安城小，都統烏蘭泰軍西南，提督向榮軍東北，合滇、黔、楚、蜀兵四萬餘人，賊數千壁險死鬥。
units.en: Yong'an was a small city; Banner Commander Ulan Tai held the southwest and Regional Commander Xiang Rong the northeast; together they had more than forty thousand troops from Yunnan, Guizhou, Huguang, and Sichuan, while several thousand rebels held the high ground and fought desperately.
units.literal: Yong'an city was small; Banner Commander Ulan Tai's army was southwest, Regional Commander Xiang Rong's army northeast; together Yunnan, Guizhou, Huguang, and Sichuan troops numbered over forty thousand; several thousand rebels held perilous positions and fought to the death.

units.zh: 水竇者，永安東北之隘也，緣山徑可達桂林。
units.en: Shuidou was the pass northeast of Yong'an; a mountain path there led to Guilin.
units.literal: Shuidou was the pass northeast of Yong'an; along mountain paths one could reach Guilin.

units.zh: 瑩與烏蘭泰皆主擊水竇，絕賊外援，向榮不從，自由龍寮嶺進而敗，乃議開水竇一路縱賊逸，尾追擊之。
units.en: Yao and Ulan Tai both urged an assault on Shuidou to cut off outside help; Xiang Rong refused, advanced by Longliao Ridge, and was defeated; the command then proposed opening Shuidou to let the rebels escape and chasing them afterward.
units.literal: Ying and Ulan Tai both favored striking Shuidou to cut off rebel outside aid; Xiang Rong would not agree, advanced freely from Longliao Ridge and was defeated; then they discussed opening the Shuidou route to let rebels escape and pursue from behind.

units.zh: 瑩力辯其失，賽尚阿仍用向榮策，賊果突圍出犯桂林，烏蘭泰戰死，賽尚阿逮問。
units.en: Yao argued strenuously against the plan, but Saišangga followed Xiang Rong's strategy; the rebels broke out, struck toward Guilin, Ulan Tai was killed in battle, and Saišangga was arrested.
units.literal: Ying strongly argued the error; Saišangga still used Xiang Rong's plan; rebels indeed broke out and attacked Guilin; Ulan Tai died in battle; Saišangga was arrested for questioning.

units.zh: 賊勢益熾，連陷興安、全州，犯湖南，遂不可製。
units.en: The rebels grew stronger still, took Xing'an and Quanzhou in succession, invaded Hunan, and were beyond control.
units.literal: Rebel power grew fiercer; they successively took Xing'an and Quanzhou, invaded Hunan, and could no longer be controlled.

units.zh: 瑩隨軍至湖南，巡撫張亮基奏署按察使，憂憤致疾，卒於官。
units.en: Yao followed the army into Hunan; Governor Zhang Liangji had him appointed acting provincial judge, but grief and anger brought on illness and he died in office.
units.literal: Ying followed the army to Hunan; Governor Zhang Liangji memorialized appointing him acting provincial judge; grief and anger brought illness, and he died in office.

units.zh: 瑩師事從祖鼐，不好經生章句，務通大意，見諸施行。
units.en: Yao studied under his collateral ancestor Yao Nai, cared little for pedantic textual scholarship, sought the larger meaning, and put it into practice.
units.literal: Ying studied under his collateral ancestor Nai, disliked classicist chapter-and-phrase learning, strove to grasp great principles, and applied them in practice.

units.zh: 文章善持論，指陳時事利害，慷慨深切。
units.en: His essays argued forcefully, analyzing current affairs with passionate conviction and depth.
units.literal: In essays he was skilled at sustaining argument, pointing out advantages and harms of current affairs with generous depth.

units.zh: 所著東溟文集、奏稿、後湘詩集、東槎紀略、康輶紀行及雜著諸書，為中復堂全集，行於世。
units.en: His works—including the Eastern Sea Collection, memorial drafts, Later Xiang Poems, Eastern Raft Notes, Journey Around Kang, and other writings—were published as the Zhongfu Hall Complete Works.
units.literal: His works Eastern Sea Collected Writings, Memorial Drafts, Later Xiang Poetry Collection, Eastern Raft Notes, Journey Around Kang and miscellaneous writings were compiled as the Zhongfu Hall Complete Works and circulated in the world.

units.zh: 子濬昌，能繼家學。
units.en: His son Junchang carried on the family's scholarly tradition.
units.literal: His son Junchang could continue the family's learning.

units.zh: 曾國籓以名家子留佐幕，官江西安福、湖北竹山知縣。
units.en: Zeng Guofan kept him on his staff as the son of a distinguished family; he served as magistrate of Anfu in Jiangxi and Zhushan in Hubei.
units.literal: Zeng Guofan kept him in his staff as son of a famous family; he served as magistrate of Anfu in Jiangxi and Zhushan in Hubei.

units.zh: 工詩，有五瑞堂集。
units.en: He was a skilled poet and left a collection entitled Wuru Hall.
units.literal: He was skilled in poetry and had the Wuru Hall Collection.

units.zh: 論曰：林培厚救荒治河有實績，而以察吏招忌。
units.en: The historians comment: Lin Peihou achieved real results in famine relief and river works, yet by reporting on subordinate officials he made powerful enemies.
units.literal: The judgment says: Lin Peihou had real achievements in famine relief and river control, yet by inspecting officials incurred resentment.

units.zh: 李宗傳便宜平夷，功在邊方。
units.en: Li Zongchuan pacified the Yi by flexible measures, and his merit lay on the frontier.
units.literal: Li Zongchuan by expedient measures pacified the Yi; his merit lay on the frontier.

units.zh: 王鳳生、俞德淵佐陶澍治淮鹽，尤濟時之才。
units.en: Wang Fengsheng and Yu Deyuan assisted Tao Shu in reforming Huai salt—men of outstanding practical talent for their time.
units.literal: Wang Fengsheng and Yu Deyuan assisted Tao Shu in governing Huai salt—especially talents who aided the age.

units.zh: 姚瑩保岩疆，挫強敵，反遭讒譴，然朝廷未嘗不諒其忠勤，海內引領望其再用，亦不可謂不遇矣。
units.en: Yao Ying defended the coastal frontier and humbled a powerful enemy, yet was slandered and punished; still the court never doubted his loyalty, and the empire looked to his recall—so one cannot say fortune wholly passed him by.
units.literal: Yao Ying defended the rocky frontier, defeated a strong enemy, yet on the contrary suffered slander and punishment; yet the court never failed to understand his loyalty and diligence; within the seas men craned their necks hoping for his reuse—it also cannot be said that he was unmet by opportunity.
